stories.headline: Aramco reports record 25% Q1 profit jump as East-West pipeline runs at full capacity amid Hormuz disruption
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco reported a 25–26% jump in Q1 2026 net profit to approximately $32–33.6 billion, beating analyst forecasts, as the company redirected crude exports through its East-West Pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu after Strait of Hormuz shipping was effectively closed by the US-Iran war. CEO Amin Nasser warned that global energy markets face disruption extending into 2027 if Hormuz flows do not resume immediately, and noted the world has lost roughly one billion barrels over two months.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia disputes Trump's unilateral Project Freedom launch, then lifts US base restrictions after tense standoff
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia and Kuwait temporarily barred US military aircraft from using their bases and airspace after President Trump launched 'Project Freedom' — an operation to escort commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz — without coordinating with Gulf allies. Following a tense call between Trump and MBS, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait lifted the restrictions, enabling the US to seek resumption of the operation. Reporting indicates Saudi officials were angered by the unannounced launch and feared it would trigger Iranian escalation against Gulf states.

stories.headline: Saudi FM conducts intensive regional diplomatic calls on Iran war and Hormuz crisis
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan engaged in a series of phone calls and meetings with counterparts across the region and beyond during the week of May 5–10, covering the US-Iran conflict, the Strait of Hormuz situation, and de-escalation efforts. His interlocutors included the Iranian, Russian, Qatari, Egyptian, Jordanian, and Japanese foreign ministers, and he participated in a MED9 Arab League video conference on Hormuz freedom of navigation.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia and Turkey sign visa exemption agreement at Coordination Council meeting in Ankara
stories.summary: Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan visited Ankara on May 6 for the third meeting of the Turkish-Saudi Coordination Council, where he and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan signed a reciprocal visa exemption agreement for diplomatic and special passport holders. Bin Farhan also met President Erdogan at the Presidential Complex. The visit was framed against the backdrop of deepening Saudi-Turkish coordination amid the Iran war.

stories.headline: UAE exits OPEC and OPEC+, sharpening Saudi-UAE tensions and straining GCC cohesion
stories.summary: The UAE announced its withdrawal from both OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, 2026 — a move that generated extensive Arabic-language analysis focused on the widening Saudi-UAE strategic rift, questions about GCC cohesion, and implications for Saudi Arabia's leadership of the oil cartel. The UAE ambassador to the US published an op-ed explaining the decision as reflecting a strategic economic shift. Coverage in both Arabic and English framed the withdrawal as part of a broader divergence between Riyadh and Abu Dhabi over production policy, the Iran war, and geopolitical ambitions.

stories.headline: PIF withdraws LIV Golf funding; league seeks new investors as players face uncertain future
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund confirmed it will end its financial backing of LIV Golf after the 2026 season, having invested over $5 billion in the breakaway circuit since 2022. LIV Golf retained law firm Gibson Dunn and investment adviser Ducera Partners to find replacement investors; CEO Scott O'Neil held a press conference addressing the transition. Players including Rory McIlroy and Joaquin Niemann publicly commented, and PIF confirmed its separate deals with TKO (WWE/UFC) and tennis would continue.

stories.headline: NEOM promoted as Red Sea logistics hub and Hormuz bypass route as megaproject scales back ambitions
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia began actively marketing NEOM's port as a multimodal logistics corridor connecting Europe, Egypt, and the Gulf — a strategic pivot driven by the Strait of Hormuz closure. Concurrently, reporting confirmed NEOM is reshaping its mission toward data centers and industrial tenants after walking back the futuristic 'Line' city concept, with the Trojena ski resort contract cancelled and PIF approving a phased delivery approach focused on financial returns.

stories.headline: PIF opens Shanghai office, issues $7bn bond drawing $14bn+ orders, and announces new three-portfolio investment structure
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund opened a second mainland China office in Shanghai earlier in 2026 to expand deal-making with Chinese investors. Separately, PIF issued a three-tranche US dollar bond this week that drew over $14 billion in orders for a $7 billion offering — its return to public debt markets after the disruption of the Iran conflict. The fund's board, chaired by MBS, also approved a 2026-2030 strategy reorganizing investments into three portfolios (Vision, Strategic, and Financial) with a greater emphasis on financial returns.

stories.headline: PIF-backed EA buyout faces protest as gamers plan raid on EA headquarters
stories.summary: A group calling itself Players Alliance HQ announced a cosplay protest at Electronic Arts' Redwood City headquarters on May 11 to oppose a pending $55 billion buyout of EA by a consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, with Silver Lake and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners holding smaller stakes. The deal, disclosed in September 2025, still requires FTC and CFIUS approval. Over three dozen US lawmakers have also raised concerns about the transaction.

stories.headline: GCC states coordinate collective response to Iranian attacks and Hormuz crisis through diplomacy and UN outreach
stories.summary: GCC member states condemned Iranian attacks on UAE and Kuwait, with the GCC Secretary-General calling the strikes a flagrant violation of sovereignty. GCC ambassadors joined the US Ambassador at the UN Security Council to call for a resolution protecting freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and GCC-EU ambassador-level dialogue was held in Geneva. MBS separately called UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed to affirm solidarity.
